newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends sharply lower on weak crude, arb.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends sharply lower on weak crude, arb.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended sharply lower on Thursday after crude's selloff the last two days and because of the lingering impact of rising U.S. inventories and a closed arbitrage to the States, traders said.
But Eurograde barges again found support near the psychological $200 a tonne level for fob ARA.
"It's fallen with the crude but it looks to have a stabilised a bit," for the near term, a broker said.
Eurograde ended $8 lower at $202/$204 fob ARA and regular unleaded fell about $7 to $198/$200, sources said.

"There is no buying right now and at this point the arbitrage window is closed," for both small and large vessels, a trader in Germany said. "The Northwest Europe market is showing more product...and we've left winter."
Traders said demand in Germany was also lacklustre.
Eurograde barges traded twice earlier at $205, then at $204 and at least twice at $203.50, traders said.
Regular unleaded traded twice at $199 fob ARA.
Both premium and regular unleaded held a contango of about $1-$2 based on the swaps and seasonal factors.
In the cargo market, a 10,000 tonne premium unleaded cargo was confirmed traded at $211 cif into Hamburg.
Cargoes ended the day at $208/$211 cif and regular unleaded at $204/$207 cif, traders said.
Texaco fixed the 60,000 tonne Adamas vessel for loading out of Pembroke, Wales, on March 3, destined for the U.S. Atlantic Coast, according to shipping sources.
